message.content:
I'm investigating how to add RV32 (D23 core) support to this hybrid RISC-V co-simulator. Currently it's RV64-focused. I need to understand the state ABI and vsim side.

Explore and report back (with file paths and line numbers):

1. Read `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` fully. Report: how are GPRs/FPRs/CSRs sized (uint64_t? uint32_t?)? How does HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 work? Is the struct XLEN-aware or does it always use 64-bit fields? Would an RV32 core's state fit/work in this struct? What would need to change for RV32?

2. The QEMU plugin: read `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`. How does it read register values (gdbstub register reads)? Does it assume 64-bit width anywhere? How does it detect XLEN? How does it set HYBRID_FLAG_RV64?

3. The vsim resume/drain side: skim `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` and `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`. Do they assume RV64 (64-bit DMI register access, mstatus width, etc)? Where would RV32 (32-bit XLEN) cause problems? Look for any XLEN/width assumptions in the DMI abstract command code.

4. The vsim CPU config: how are vsim CPU variants configured (the VSIM_CONFIG_FILE / config.yaml mentioned in CLAUDE.md)? Is there any existing RV32 config? Where do the verilator CPU binaries come from (e.g. sim_ax45mpv_premium)? Is D23 or any rv32 variant present anywhere? grep for "d23", "D23", "rv32".

Report concisely with file:line references. Do NOT modify any files - this is read-only exploration.

content.text: I'll conduct a systematic exploration of the hybrid RISC-V co-simulator to understand RV32 support requirements. Let me start with the key files.

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 2 (L11): vreg[] widened from 64 to 128 bytes per register, which
25	// shifts every field after it. Readers reject version-1 files loudly (all
26	// three consumers check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
27	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2u
28	
29	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 (1u << 0)
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP   (1u << 1)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V    (1u << 2)
32	
33	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
34	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
35	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
36	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
37	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
38	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
39	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
40	
41	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
42	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
43	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
44	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
45	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
46	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
47	
48	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
49	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
50	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
51	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
52	
53	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
54	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
55	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
56	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
57	  uint32_t magic;
58	  uint32_t version;
59	  uint32_t flags;
60	  uint32_t hart_id;
61	  uint64_t pc;
62	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
63	
64	  uint64_t gpr[32];
65	  uint64_t fpr[32];
66	
67	  uint64_t mstatus;
68	  uint64_t mepc;
69	  uint64_t mtvec;
70	  uint64_t mcause;
71	  uint64_t mtval;
72	  uint64_t mscratch;
73	  uint64_t medeleg;
74	  uint64_t mideleg;
75	  uint64_t mip;
76	  uint64_t mie;
77	  uint64_t mcycle;
78	  uint64_t minstret;
79	  uint64_t satp;
80	
81	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
82	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
83	
84	  uint64_t vstart;
85	  uint64_t vtype;
86	  uint64_t vl;
87	  uint64_t vlenb;
88	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
89	  uint64_t vxsat;
90	  uint64_t vxrm;
91	  uint64_t vcsr;
92	
93	  // F13: warmup-window snapshot of cycle/instret counters, captured K insns
94	  // after vsim entry. Drain-only metadata; ResumeDriver never restores them.
95	  // Both zero when --vsim-warmup-icount=0 or the workload exited inside the
96	  // warmup window. Consumes 16 bytes from the original 232-byte reserved tail.
97	  uint64_t mcycle_at_measure_start;
98	  uint64_t minstret_at_measure_start;
99	
100	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
101	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
102	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
103	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
104	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
105	  uint64_t fcsr;
106	
107	  // Andes machine-setup CSRs: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches,
108	  // mmisc_ctl (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. crt0 writes them once at
109	  // boot; transporting them keeps the cycle engine from resuming caches-off
110	  // (ResumeDriver has the full rationale). Drained by the plugin, restored by
111	  // ResumeDriver, but NOT re-read by StateDrain: they are boot-static and the
112	  // drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg). Old state files carry 0 here
113	  // (reset value), which is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump.
114	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
115	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
116	
117	  uint8_t  reserved[192];  // zero-initialise on write; 256 - 3*8 (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) - 2*8 (warmup) - 8 (fcsr) - 2*8 (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)
118	};
119	
120	#ifdef __cplusplus
121	}  // extern "C"
122	#endif
123	
124	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
125	
126	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	**Primary path (`./andes-sim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
20	first use), used in all user-facing docs. The retired Python driver is kept
21	as `hsim.py`, the byte-parity golden (`tests/andes_sim/parity.sh`); the
22	SimPoint pipeline (`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`,
23	`archive`, `replay`) still runs only there until the C++ port lands.
24	
25	```sh
26	./andes-sim build                  # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
27	./andes-sim test                   # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
28	./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>
29	./andes-sim list <models|engines>
30	```
31	
32	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
33	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
34	
35	```sh
36	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
37	source ./setup.sh
38	
39	# Build individual components
40	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
41	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
42	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT="$PWD/QEMU"  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree); QEMU_ROOT must be absolute (make -C chdirs first)
43	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
44	
45	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
46	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
47	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
48	
49	# Clean
50	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
51	```
52	
53	**Outputs:**
54	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
55	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
56	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
57	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
58	
59	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
60	
61	## Running Tests
62	
63	```sh
64	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
65	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
66	
67	# Run with specific options
68	JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
69	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
70	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
71	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
72	
73	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
74	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
75	# To run ctest directly after build:
76	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
77	```
78	
79	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
80	
81	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
82	
83	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver (parity vs the golden + feature contracts); `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are the retired golden's own per-feature smoke tests (they now invoke `hsim.py`). Both families run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
84	
85	## Architecture
86	
87	### Two-Phase Handoff
88	
89	```
90	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
91	```
92	
93	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
94	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
95	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
96	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
97	
98	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
99	
100	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
101	
102	### Trigger Modes
103	
104	The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.
105	
106	Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
107	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>` (`andes_sim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
108	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
109	
110	Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
111	- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads.
112	- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
113	
114	`./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc|icount` is the unified orchestrator (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` for SimPoint); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
115	
116	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
117	
118	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
119	
120	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
121	
122	### V-State Transport
123	
124	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
125	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
126	ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
127	maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
128	scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
129	program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
130	image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
131	required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
132	with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
133	Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
134	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
135	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
136	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
137	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
138	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
139	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
140	
141	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
142	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
143	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
144	runtime vlenb.
145	
146	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
147	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
148	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
149	
150	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
151	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
152	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
153	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
154	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
155	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
156	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
157	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
158	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
159	
160	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
161	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
162	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
163	
164	### Test Fixtures
165	
166	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
167	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
168	the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:
169	
170	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
171	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
172	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
173	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
174	| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `--what runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |
175	
176	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
177	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
178	
179	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andes_sim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.
180	
181	### vsim CMake Structure
182	
183	vsim lives entirely in `verilator/`. Key CMake options:
184	- `VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID` (default OFF) - enables e2e CTest registration
185	- `VSIM_CONFIG_FILE` - CPU YAML (default `config.yaml`)
186	- `VSIM_NO_VERILATOR` - skip Verilator build (assume prebuilt)
187	
188	The hybrid orchestration layer (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`) is header-only and depends only on C++20 standard library + the shared ABI header. SystemC/Verilator are not required for hybrid unit tests.
189	
190	Hybrid unit tests (`tests/hybrid/`) use [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest). They are registered in `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` and run via `ctest`. The `recording_bus.hpp` pattern provides a duck-typed test double for the DMI bus without requiring virtual interfaces.
191	
192	## Key Files
193	
194	| File | Purpose |
195	|------|---------|
196	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
197	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
198	| `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` | Phase dispatcher |
199	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
200	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | DMI state capture |
201	| `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` | V register transport via scratch region |
202	| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` | CTest registration for all e2e fixtures |
203	| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
204	| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |
